answer.rationale: Rollback is excluded by compliance despite memory_b1's precedent, since the security patch must stay. The degradation is confined to the primary region and driven by heavy write load during settlement peak, so regional_failover (memory_b2) risks write consistency/loss if replication lag or split-brain occurs under heavy write traffic — verifying that memory is needed to check whether it addressed write-path safety or only read/error-rate recovery. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing (memory_b4, memory_b5) don't target the actual bottleneck: sustained write-path latency from load, not a failing dependency or read contention. Provisioning additional headroom (memory_b3) directly matches a prior precedent for absorbing surge-driven queue growth without touching routing or the release, minimizing risk to in-flight writes. I verify memory_b3 to confirm the precedent generalizes to write-path saturation (not just read/queue systems) and memory_b2 to rule out failover as a safer alternative given write-safety concerns.
